topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of the lecture, outlines the focus on inflammation initiation and resolution, and explains how the session builds on prior knowledge.

topics.label: Principles of Innate Immune Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts of innate immune sensing, including how molecular patterns of pathogens and tissue damage are distinguished from self and detected by host receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the major classes of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling cascades, and the activation of downstream inflammatory pathways such as the inflammasome.

topics.label: Acute Inflammatory Cascade and Cell Trafficking
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the cellular and systemic progression of acute inflammation, showing how local immune activation coordinates leukocyte movement and can escalate into systemic disease.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation and Tissue Repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the immune system terminates inflammation and repairs damaged tissue, as well as the chronic inflammatory and containment states that occur when resolution is incomplete.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the subject of the upcoming lecture.
